dashboard_subtitle: North-Western Sahara Aquifer System — Decision-support tool
header_programme: Sahara and Sahel Observatory — Watch & Outlook Programme
header_description: Transforming GRACE/GRACE-FO satellite data into readable indicators, long-term trend, and short-term forecast for transboundary water governance.
kpi_anomaly_context: Last observed month deviation from the 2004–2009 baseline
kpi_trend_rate_context: Sen's slope on observed months only (imputed excluded)
kpi_trend_vol_context: The observed deficit is 2–3× the net deficit estimated by OSS (~1–2 km³/yr). GRACE measures total storage change, not net abstraction.
kpi_forecast_context: Rolling-origin CV validated (MAE ≈ 6 mm). Gap vs. last observed month.
kpi_vigilance_context: Based on z-score vs. 2004–2009 baseline (z < −2 = High, −2 ≤ z < −1 = Moderate)
kpi_mk_context: Seasonal Mann-Kendall test on observed months only (imputed excluded)
proxy_warning_text: Groundwater storage is approximated as GRACE total water storage minus GLDAS-modelled surface stores. This is a first-order separation for trend visualisation — not validated against in-situ piezometry.
metadata_text: Area: SASS — Algeria, Tunisia, Libya | Source: GRACE/GRACE-FO JPL Mascons (CRI) | Unit: mm (water equivalent), km³
ts_title: Groundwater storage has declined steadily since 2002
ts_context: Observed GWSA proxy (GRACE minus GLDAS surface stores) with uncertainty band, trend line, and forecast fan chart. The 2017–2018 inter-mission gap is interpolated and flagged.
ts_decision_bullet_1: A synthetic indicator of groundwater stock status at basin scale
ts_decision_bullet_2: A trend converted to a governance-ready unit: km³/yr
ts_decision_bullet_3: A forecast with uncertainty, instead of a simple descriptive curve
ts_decision_bullet_4: Full transparency on GRACE/GRACE-FO data gaps and imputed months
annual_bar_title: Year after year, the deficit deepens
annual_bar_context: Annual mean of the groundwater storage anomaly (observed months only). Partial years shown in lighter tone. The steady downward staircase confirms the long-term depletion trend.
trend_detail_title: Two methods converge: the SASS loses ~4–5 mm/yr of equivalent water
trend_detail_context: Comparison with OSS expected net deficit: ~1–2 km³/yr (recharge ~1 vs. abstraction ~2.5–3.1 km³/yr). GRACE measures total storage change, which exceeds the net deficit because it includes inter-annual variability.
stl_title: Trend dominates: seasonality is virtually absent on this fossil basin
stl_context: The near-absence of seasonality confirms the fossil character of the SASS — depletion is driven by abstraction, not climate.
stl_explanation: STL decomposes the signal into three components. On the SASS, the trend component captures nearly all variability — the seasonal cycle is negligible, confirming that depletion is driven by abstraction from a fossil aquifer, not by climate.
seasonal_bar_title: The seasonal cycle is negligible — depletion is abstraction-driven, not climate-driven
seasonal_bar_context: Average monthly deviation from the annual mean (STL seasonal component). The near-flat profile confirms the fossil character of the SASS — unlike recharged Sahelian aquifers where a clear wet-season signal would appear.
gldas_bar_title: The surface component (GLDAS) accounts for less than 15% of total signal variability
gldas_bar_context: Standard deviation of each component over observed months. The GWSA proxy inherits most of its variability from GRACE total water storage, with a small surface correction from GLDAS.
scenario_title: Depletion is projected to continue over the next five years
scenario_context: Prophet forecast with rolling-origin cross-validation. Validated horizon: 24 months (MAE ≈ 6 mm). Beyond that, scenario extrapolation under current conditions — NOT a validated forecast.
forecast_detail_title: 24-month forecast validated (MAE ≈ 6 mm) — beyond that, exploratory scenario
forecast_detail_context: Rolling-origin cross-validation confirms forecast skill up to 24 months (MAE ≈ 6.1 mm). Beyond 24 months, projections assume trend continuation under current conditions — they are scenarios, NOT validated forecasts.
map_title: SASS aquifer extent and GRACE mascon grid
decision_depletion_text: The SASS aquifer system has lost approximately {anomaly} of equivalent water height since 2004–2009 (Mann-Kendall p {pvalue}).
decision_forecast_text: Trend continuation with MAE ≈ 6.1 mm. Beyond 24 months, projections are scenario extrapolations with reduced confidence.
decision_fossil_text: Rainfall shows negligible coupling with storage change at basin scale — the depletion is abstraction-driven, not climate-driven.
decision_resolution_text: GRACE mascons (~300 km) support basin-scale aggregates only — sub-basin or per-country splits are indicative, not quantitative.
method_title: From satellite measurement to groundwater proxy: a reproducible pipeline
method_context: The pipeline is fully automated and reproducible from raw GRACE/GLDAS data to the static dashboard.
method_pipeline_text: The pipeline proceeds in seven stages: (1) GRACE JPL mascon fields (RL06.3 V04, CRI-filtered) are loaded as monthly total water storage anomalies in cm. (2) The field is clipped to the SASS aquifer boundary (GeoJSON polygon). (3) GLDAS-2.1 Noah surface stores (soil moisture across four layers, snow water equivalent, canopy interception) are subtracted after re-baselining to the same 2004–2009 reference period. (4) The resulting groundwater storage anomaly proxy (GWSA, in mm) is assembled with uncertainty estimates and imputation flags. (5) Trend analysis applies OLS regression with Newey-West standard errors and the seasonal Mann-Kendall test; STL decomposition separates trend, seasonality, and residual. (6) Prophet generates forecasts with rolling-origin cross-validation; horizons beyond 24 months are labelled as exploratory scenarios. (7) This static HTML dashboard is rendered via Jinja2 with client-side Plotly charts.
method_limit_1: Spatial resolution ~300 km (mascons) — basin-scale aggregates only
method_limit_2: Prototype proxy not validated against in-situ piezometry
method_limit_3: Forecasts assume stationarity — cannot anticipate policy or pumping shifts
method_limit_4: 2017–2018 inter-mission gap filled by interpolation (flagged in all analyses)
method_limit_5: Non-separability of Continental Intercalaire and Complexe Terminal aquifers at this resolution
method_limit_6: Saharan chotts (Jerid, Melrhir) contribute an unmodelled surface-water signal that remains in the proxy
scenario_multi_title: Three possible trajectories over the next five years
scenario_multi_context: Trend continuation is the central scenario. Dry-year and enhanced-management scenarios bound the range of possibilities — these are not validated forecasts.
decision_monitoring_text: A consolidated monthly signal for the SASS. GRACE monthly frequency enables near-real-time tracking of the storage anomaly at basin scale.
decision_anticipation_text: Visualize multiple possible trajectories over 24 to 60 months. The validated horizon (24 months, MAE ≈ 6 mm) provides a reliable projection; beyond, scenarios frame the uncertainty.
decision_dialogue_text: An objective basis for exchanges between concerned countries. GRACE indicators are independent of national declarations — a neutral reference point for the tripartite Consultation Mechanism.
decision_capitalisation_text: Prepare a future extension to other transboundary aquifers. The pipeline is designed to be applied to ITTAS and other systems in the OSS portfolio.
decision_limits_inline: Integrated limitations: coarse GRACE resolution (~300 km), basin-scale interpretation only. TWSA − GLDAS approximation not validated in situ. Inter-mission gap 2017–2018 interpolated. CI/CT non-separability at this resolution.
decision_utility_text: Transform a complex satellite dataset into a readable, reproducible, and shareable institutional tool for the strategic monitoring of the SASS.
footer_credits: Data: NASA/JPL GRACE mascons (RL06.3 V04, CRI) · GLDAS-2.1 Noah · OSS SASS programme
footer_version: Pipeline v0.1.0 — Static dashboard generated by Jinja2 + Plotly
vigilance_explain_high: z-score below −2 — the current anomaly is exceptionally low relative to the 2004–2009 baseline. Immediate attention recommended.
vigilance_explain_moderate: z-score between −2 and −1 — the anomaly is significantly below the baseline. Enhanced monitoring advised.
vigilance_explain_low: z-score above −1 — the anomaly is within the normal range of variability.
tooltip_gwsa: Groundwater Storage Anomaly — deviation of estimated groundwater storage from the 2004–2009 mean, in mm of equivalent water height.
tooltip_twsa: Total Water Storage Anomaly — the full signal measured by GRACE satellites, including all water stores (ground, surface, soil, snow).
tooltip_stl: Seasonal-Trend decomposition using Loess — a statistical method that separates a time series into trend, seasonal, and residual components.
tooltip_mk: Mann-Kendall — a non-parametric test for monotonic trends in time series data. Does not assume normality.
tooltip_hac: Heteroskedasticity and Autocorrelation Consistent — a correction applied to standard errors to account for serial correlation in time series regression.
tooltip_zscore: z-score — number of standard deviations the current value is from the mean. A z-score of −2 means the value is 2 standard deviations below average.
tooltip_mascon: Mass Concentration block — GRACE data is delivered as ~300 km grid cells, each representing average water storage change over that area.
expert_scenario_title: Detailed scenario analysis with confidence intervals
expert_scenario_context: Three scenarios projected over 60 months. Each scenario shows its own prediction interval. The dry-year scenario assumes 50% acceleration of the current decline; enhanced management assumes 50% reduction.
expert_gldas_title: Signal decomposition: GRACE vs GLDAS contribution
expert_gldas_context: GWSA is derived as TWSA (GRACE) minus GLDAS surface stores (soil moisture, SWE, canopy). On the SASS, the surface correction is small: GLDAS accounts for less than 15% of total signal variability, confirming that the GWSA proxy inherits most of its signal from GRACE total water storage. This is consistent with the fossil character of the aquifer — minimal surface water dynamics.
